events.quote: Ferdinand Schörner ( 12 June 1892 – 2 July 1973 ) was a German general

events.quote: Ferdinand Schörner ( 12 June 1892 – 2 July 1973 ) was a German general

events.text: At his death in 1973 he was the last living German field marshal.

events.quote: At his death in 1973 he was the last living German field marshal .

events.text: Schörner was born in Munich, Kingdom of Bavaria, German Empire.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Schörner was born on 12 June 1892 in Munich

events.text: He entered the Prussian Army as a one-year volunteer with the Bavarian Leib Regiment.
events.subject: self
events.quote: He entered the Prussian Army in October 1911 as a one-year volunteer with the Bavarian Leib Regiment

events.text: He was a Leutnant der Reserve.
events.subject: self
events.quote: by November 1914 he was a Leutnant der Reserve

events.text: He was awarded the Pour le Mérite military order as a lieutenant when he took part in the Battle of Caporetto.
events.subject: self
events.quote: he was awarded the Pour le Mérite military order as a lieutenant when he took part in the Battle of Caporetto

events.text: He was adjutant to General Otto von Lossow, the commander of Wehrkreis VII in Munich.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1923 he was adjutant to General Otto von Lossow

events.text: He participated in the defeat of the Beer Hall Putsch.
events.subject: self
events.quote: participated in the defeat of the Beer Hall Putsch

events.text: Schörner commanded the 98th Mountain Regiment in the invasion of Poland.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Schörner commanded the 98th Mountain Regiment in the invasion of Poland in 1939

events.text: During the 1941 Balkans campaign, Schörner commanded the German 6th Mountain Division.
events.subject: self
events.quote: During the 1941 Balkans campaign , he commanded the German 6th Mountain Division

events.text: Schörner took part in Operation Barbarossa with the 6th Mountain Division.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Schörner took part in Operation Barbarossa in June 1941

events.text: As a General der Gebirgstruppe, Schörner took command of the XIX Mountain Corps.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1942 as a General der Gebirgstruppe he took command of the XIX Mountain Corps

events.text: Schörner was promoted to the rank of Generalleutnant.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In February 1942 , Schörner was promoted to the rank of Generalleutnant

events.text: Schörner commanded the XXXX Panzer Corps on the Eastern Front.
events.subject: self
events.quote: He later commanded the XXXX Panzer Corps on the Eastern Front from November 1943 to January 1944

events.text: Schörner's command of the XXXX Panzer Corps ended.
events.subject: self
events.quote: from November 1943 to January 1944

events.text: Schörner was made commander of Army Group A.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In March 1944 he was made commander of Army Group A

events.text: Schörner became commander of Army Group South Ukraine.
events.subject: self
events.quote: and in May commander of Army Group South Ukraine

events.text: During the late spring, Schörner oversaw the retreat from the Dniester River in Romania.
events.subject: self
events.quote: During the late spring of 1944 , Schörner oversaw the retreat from the Dniester River in Romania

events.text: Schörner was promoted to the rank of Generaloberst.

events.text: Schörner became commander of Army Group North.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In July he became commander of Army Group North

events.text: Schörner stayed in command until he was made commander of Army Group Centre.
events.subject: self
events.quote: where he stayed until January 1945 when he was made commander of Army Group Centre

events.text: Schörner was made commander of Army Group Centre, defending Czechoslovakia and the upper reaches of the River Oder.

events.text: Schörner was promoted to field marshal.

events.quote: On 5 April 1945 , Schörner was promoted to field marshal

events.text: Schörner was named as the new Commander-in-Chief of the German Army High Command (OKH).
events.subject: self
events.quote: was named as the new Commander-in-Chief of the German Army High Command ( OKH )

events.text: Schörner nominally served in this post until the surrender of the Third Reich.
events.subject: self
events.object: Commander-in-Chief of the German Army High Command

events.text: The last the OKW had heard from Schörner was on 2 May.

events.text: Schörner deserted and flew to Austria.

events.text: Schörner was arrested by the Americans.
events.subject: self
events.quote: where he was arrested by the Americans on 18 May

events.text: Units of Army Group Centre capitulated.
events.subject: part_of_self
events.quote: Units of Army Group Centre , the last big German units to surrender , capitulated on 11 May 1945

events.text: Schörner handed himself in to the Americans.
events.subject: self
events.quote: on 18 May 1945 Schörner handed himself in to the Americans

events.text: Schörner was charged with war crimes.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In August 1951 he was charged with war crimes

events.text: The Military Board of the Soviet Supreme Court sentenced Schörner to 25 years imprisonment.
events.subject: self
events.quote: in February 1952 the Military Board of the Soviet Supreme Court sentenced him to 25 years imprisonment

events.text: A decree of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet reduced his sentence to 12 and a half years.
events.subject: self
events.quote: A decree of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet in April 1952 reduced this sentence to 12 and a half years

events.text: A decree allowed Schörner to be handed over to authorities of East Germany.
